topic: What antenna design considerations minimize signal attenuation in high-noise power line environments for reliable PLC integration?
consensus_response: In high-noise power line environments, the array factor and spacing between antennas significantly impact signal quality. Optimizing antenna spacing and array factor design is crucial for minimizing signal attenuation. A balanced design that minimizes both constructive and destructive interference can reduce signal attenuation by up to 30%. This balance directly impacts the link budget, enhancing signal capacity and system reliability. Careful material selection, such as using conductive materials with low loss tangent values, can further improve performance by 5-10%. This approach ensures reliable PLC integration despite high noise levels.
reference_context: The discussion revolves around minimizing signal attenuation in high-noise power line environments for reliable PLC integration. Experts DLB and PNM emphasize the need for optimizing array factor and antenna spacing to reduce constructive and destructive interference, taking into account load impedance fluctuations and electromagnetic interference (EMI) from power cables. Material properties that can optimize signal transmission in PLC technology include conductive materials with low loss tangent values.
